discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and moire quantum matter
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. These results created a new field. A single, cleanly tunable material now shows the main phenomena of strongly correlated quantum matter: Mott-like insulators, unconventional superconducting domes, strange-metal linear-in-temperature resistivity, orbital magnetism and quantum anomalous Hall states. Previously these were studied only in chemically complex compounds such as the cuprates. The discovery turned the twist angle into a control parameter for quantum phases. It started the worldwide program of moire materials, which led to the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect, and it opened a direct experimental path to the deepest open problems of entangled quantum matter.
